title: Dalal Street Week Ahead: Inflation, Earnings and Foreign Flows Decide the Rally
excerpt: After the Nifty reclaimed 25,000 on a Rs 45,960 crore foreign buying week, a holiday-shortened week brings India and US inflation prints, continuing Q2 earnings and a test of whether foreign flows hold.
body:
• Indian markets are closed on Monday, November 9 for Bali Pratipada, making this a holiday-shortened trading week, according to Outlook Money.
  • India's October retail inflation data is due November 12 and US October CPI on November 10 — the two prints most likely to move rate expectations this week.
  • Foreign investors bought a net Rs 45,960.02 crore in the cash segment in November after selling a net Rs 45,161.71 crore in October; domestic investors sold a net Rs 24,196.52 crore in November.
  • For NRI portfolios: the rally into Diwali rested on that foreign reversal, so daily flow data, not index levels alone, is the number to track this week.

Dalal Street opens the week in an unusual position: the hard part — reclaiming lost ground — is done, and the question now is what holds it up. On Friday, November 6, the Nifty 50 closed at 25,030.35, up 493.75 points or 2.01%, and the Sensex closed at 81,028.02, up 1,718.01 points or 2.17%. Moneycontrol's week-ahead preview puts Q2 earnings, US and India inflation, foreign flow and oil prices among the ten factors that will set the tone.

A shortened week, two inflation prints

Trading is compressed from the start: markets remain closed on Monday, November 9 on account of Bali Pratipada. Into the remaining sessions land two inflation releases. US October CPI, due November 10, will be read for whether inflation is cooling fast enough to support further Federal Reserve rate reductions. India's October retail inflation follows on November 12, the domestic print that frames the Reserve Bank's next decision and the rupee's direction.

The flow reversal under the rally

The week's rally was not a domestic story alone. Foreign institutional investors recorded a net purchase of Rs 45,960.02 crore in the cash segment in November, a sharp reversal from a net sale of Rs 45,161.71 crore in October. Domestic institutional investors moved the other way, logging a net sale of Rs 24,196.52 crore in November after a net purchase of Rs 62,220.11 crore the previous month. When the marginal buyer changes identity that completely in a month, the sustainability question is straightforward: do foreign buyers keep showing up after the festival week, or was this positioning around Diwali?

Earnings and oil complete the list

The September-quarter earnings season continues through the week, keeping stock-specific moves likely even if the indices consolidate. Crude oil prices remain on the watch list for their direct line into India's import bill and imported inflation. Taken together, the calendar gives the rally three separate tests — inflation, earnings and flows — inside four trading sessions.

What to watch

US CPI on Tuesday, India CPI on Thursday, and the daily foreign flow figures in between. A week that holds 25,000 on the Nifty through those prints, with foreign buying intact, reads very differently from one that gives the level back on the first soft session.
